pass_b_english: Cyril: …spoken already, and, as I myself somehow think, sufficiently the things upon the linen and the purple, and the spun scarlet, and indeed also hyacinth, we will push aside the same-speaking; yet that at least we will say for the present: The veil upon four golden pillars, whose bases are silver, was then hinting the mystery of Christ. For what? Did not wise Paul also name for us Christ’s body a veil, saying thus, ‘Which he inaugurated for us a fresh and living way through the veil, that is, of his flesh’ (Hebrews 10:20)?

Cyril: Observe then as in shadows and riddles, that being God and from God Father according to nature the Word has come to be as in a golden and undecaying ark, the temple from Virgin; for undecaying and honored is Christ’s body; and he was all but also being hidden as in an order of a veil, having taken the flesh; and we say the Word from God is hidden, not as having been limited in a small body; for everywhere and in all things is the Son; but by escaping notice economically, and enduring the time of the showing-forth. And the time of showing-forth unto all is the living-again from dead ones. For before the honored cross, he was ordering the holy disciples that they not make him apparent. For it has been written thus. And after at least living again having suffered the death, ‘Going,’ he says, ‘disciple all the nations, baptizing them unto the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the holy Spirit.’ (Matthew 17:9) So then the veil was hanging upon the pillars, covering within the ark, and it would be a type of Christ, being raised high by the proclamations of the holy evangelists, and being seen in glory of godhead by those in the holy tent—that is, the Church. And four are the pillars, golden and silver-around; and equal in number to them are the evangelists, bright and honored. So then the ark was lying, and from above downward the veil was extending, the one from linen and purple and the others, and it was making it not visible. And from above the veil and of the Cherubim unto right and left, God was naming, showing that he is also beyond every creation; and also all the uppermost of the rational ones—that is, the Seraphim—sit under the divine and ineffable glory, and escorting the Son himself, even if he has become flesh, and as somehow in a lowering of the equality toward the Father, according as he has been born human. Therefore also he himself was saying: ‘My Father is greater than I.’ (John 14:28) And being equal according to nature to the one who has begotten, he says the coming-to-be in lesser things through only the human. On account of this also in the holy tent, in a circle of the veil, the Cherubim, and they themselves escorting the Son as God. And indeed also from above the veil itself, which was unto a type of Christ, God is thought. ‘And I will be known,’ (Exodus 25:22) he says, ‘from there, and I will speak to you.’ (Matthew 28:19) For beyond every creation is the Father, and of Emmanuel himself, not according as he is thought and is God; for he is equal according to all things to God; but as far as
